statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail holds 18 because the completed US cash session retraced in both directions and the new Globex session is holding a roughly 50-point range near 30,693 rather than extending. Stress eases to 69 as WTI settles at $89.38, down 3.5% on Saudi supply relief, and the 2-year yield slips to 4.88% after Williams signalled no urgency, while a 30-year yield at 5.62% keeps the long end at a 24-year high.
recommendation: Tail remains in the low band, so the mapped state stays EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The published danger window is narrow and sits on 30 September between 12:00Z and 15:00Z, where ADP, the August PCE deflators and the final Q2 GDP estimate precede the US cash open and Chicago PMI. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Cash NDX closed 30,339.33, up 0.21%, with both its opening gap and its 30,235.67 downside probe retraced; NQ holds a roughly 50-point reopen range near 30,693 and VIX 16.04 keeps Tail at 18, while a 5.62% 30-year yield and 81.9 consumer confidence hold Stress at 69
body:
The strongest current evidence remains the completed US cash session. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,339.33, up 62.52 points or 0.21%, from a 30,276.81 prior close. It opened at 30,412.29, printed a 30,429.97 high, sold back through the prior close to a 30,235.67 low, then recovered 103.66 points to finish green. The 194.30-point range is 0.64% of index level and, decisively for this score, retracement worked in both directions: the opening gap was retraced and the downside probe was retraced in turn. That is the structural opposite of the persistent no-retracement path Tail is designed to measure.

The evening futures session reopened at 22:00Z and has so far traded a roughly 50-point band, opening at 30,657.25 and quoting near 30,693.50, up about 0.26%. A 0.16% range with no extension attempt is consistent with range-holding rather than one-way structure. VIX is 16.04, down 0.19% and near the low end of a 15.73-16.44 session range, which does not support a volatility-expansion regime.

Cross-asset evidence is genuinely two-sided, which is why Stress stays high at 69 while Tail stays low at 18. On the stressful side, the 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.62%, its highest since 2002, and the 10-year traded near 5.26-5.28%. Conference Board consumer confidence fell 6.7 points to 81.9, the lowest since 2014 and well under a 89.2 consensus, with the Expectations Index at 63.6 and 12-month inflation expectations up to 6.1%. JOLTS job openings fell to 7.079 million from 7.335 million. On the relieving side, WTI settled at $89.38, down 3.5%, after Saudi Arabia restored about half the capacity of its East-West pipeline, Hormuz transit resumed and the US released up to 40 million barrels from emergency reserves. The 2-year yield eased to 4.88% after New York Fed President Williams said there is no need for urgency on the next hike, which pared October FOMC odds to roughly even.

Breadth evidence is split rather than aligned. Latest-session, non-real-time context showed four of eight megacaps higher with dispersion near 1.5%, and two-sided semiconductor moves. Index performance also diverged, with the Nasdaq-100 up 0.21% while the Dow fell 0.26% and the S&P 500 fell 0.17%. Conflicting breadth of this kind reduces directional conviction and belongs in Stress and Confidence, not in Tail.

No current amplifier stack is observed: there is no shallow-pullback pattern with repeated extension, NQ is not pinned at a session extreme, volatility is contained, and the live oil and front-end inputs are easing rather than building. Tail therefore holds 18 in the low band and the mapping produces EA_ON. Confidence is 88 because current index, futures, volatility, yield, oil, consumer-confidence and calendar evidence was verified directly; the shared market-context file was about 165 minutes old and partial, so it was treated as stale supporting context only and was not relied on for price-path conclusions.

The published danger window is narrow and sits on 30 September from 12:00Z to 15:00Z, spanning ADP at 12:15Z, the August PCE deflators and final Q2 GDP at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open and Chicago PMI at 13:45Z. That stack is the only hour set where the forecast leaves the watch band, peaking at Tail 25 in the 13:00Z hour. It is a conditional scenario allowance for a delayed second leg meeting opening-auction continuation, not an assertion that such a path has formed.

lookbackSummary: 23 of the 24 preceding hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 14:00 UTC slot on 29 September is unavailable because no assessment was published inside that clock hour. Tail ranged from 17 to 24 and never left the low or watch bands. It troughed at 17 through the late Monday overnight, printed 24 in the 01:00, 03:00, 04:00 and 15:00 UTC hours on trend-down readings, held 20 to 21 through the European and US sessions, then eased to 19 and 18 after the US cash close. Stress fell steadily from 79 in the early Tuesday hours to 70 by 21:00 UTC as oil retreated and the front end repriced. Confidence stayed between 86 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The published forecast opens at Tail 18 for the current post-close hour, where the resolved two-way cash path and the tight Globex reopen range are actually observed, and holds 18 through the late US evening and the first Asian hours. It edges to 19 across the Asian session as verified price-path evidence ages, enters the watch band at 20 with the European pre-open and peaks at 21 around the European cash open. The conditional peak is the 13:00 UTC hour on 30 September at Tail 25, the only slot mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES, where post-PCE price discovery overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC Chicago PMI. Tail then decays through the US afternoon to 20, ticks to 21 for the quarter-end power hour and returns to the low band at 19 for the final post-close hour. Every forecast hour after the current one frames structure conditionally; no future price path or release outcome is treated as observed.
